=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:141-145,1460-1476 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The header comment (lines 141-145) and the inline comment (lines 1469-1472) say only two causes lead to the plain fallback: a rejected delta dispatch, or a transient delta failure that used up the shared retry budget. The `else` branch at lines 1468-1476 takes the fallback after any failed delta dispatch, including `auth` and `other` failures, which are not retried.
  WHY: This is a documentation error, not a runtime failure. A maintainer would expect `auth`/`other` failures to skip the fallback, but the code still makes one more `gh workflow run` call and logs `outcome=delta_fallback ... dispatch_error=auth`. All three reviewers rated it NIT, mapped here to low.
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:363-385 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: After a `network`-classified failure, the `single_pass_dispatch_audit` retry loop sends `gh workflow run` again without checking whether GitHub accepted the first dispatch.
  WHY: The per-PR concurrency group in .github/workflows/security-audit.yml:86-96 allows one running and one pending run, so the retry can queue a second audit for the same PR and use more audit and runner capacity. Severity disagreement: openai_gpt-6-luna rated it MAJOR (mapped to high); z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rated it NIT as bounded waste that the issue's Risks section accepts.
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:1438 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: In single_pass_dispatch_audit, after a transient failure such as a network timeout, the retry runs without checking whether GitHub received and processed the first request.
  WHY: The workflow concurrency group allows one running and one pending run with `cancel-in-progress: false` and does not deduplicate them, so a retry can queue a second audit for the same PR. The source rated it MAJOR, mapped to high. It has the same root cause as the 363-385 entry but cites a non-overlapping line, so it is not merged.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: G3 from issue #10104: "The sentence about an old consumer wrapper appears only for `rejected`."
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh, the exhausted-retry comment body template ("Single-issue security pass: retry audit" branch)
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The exhausted-retry branch (scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:1479-1482 per gemini; around lines 1476-1483 per minimax; lines 1488-1490 per glm) inserts `dispatch_error_sentence` but never defines or appends `dispatch_wrapper_hint`. The non-exhausted branch gates the hint on `dispatch_error_class = rejected` (:1495 per gemini; around 1493-1496 per minimax; 1502-1506 per glm). So a `rejected` failure on the exhausted-head path gets no wrapper-hint sentence. The asymmetry existed before this PR.
- requirement: Documentation accuracy: the header comment for the delta fallback should match the control flow at lines 1460-1474.
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh header comment, "Delta dispatch (gate)" paragraph (lines 139-148 and 167-173)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The header comment says "A rejected delta dispatch (a consumer wrapper without the inputs), or a transient delta failure that used up the shared retry budget, is retried once with today's arguments". The `else` branch at lines 1460-1474 has no `dispatch_error_class` gate, so `auth`, `other`, or a `rejected` failure not caused by the wrapper also falls back.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:Lines 141-145 of the header comment; code at lines 1468-1476 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The comment says only two causes lead to the plain fallback ("A rejected delta dispatch (a consumer wrapper without the inputs), or a transient delta failure that used up the shared retry budget, is retried once with today's arguments"). The code takes the fallback after any failed delta dispatch: `auth` (HTTP 401, or 403 without a rate-limit message) and `other` (for example HTTP 409, or empty output) return 1 at once, and the `else` branch at line 1468 logs `outcome=delta_fallback ... dispatch_error=<class>` (line 1473) and makes the plain call (line 1474). The comment also disagrees with line 170 ("A failed delta dispatch adds one dispatch"), and the inline comment at lines 1469-1472 has the same narrow wording.
  WHY: Nothing breaks at runtime; only the comment is wrong. It can mislead someone reading logs or tightening the classifier later. Suggested fix: reword lines 141-143 and lines 1469-1471 to "Any failed delta dispatch (for example a consumer wrapper without the inputs, or a transient failure that used up the shared retry budget) is retried once with today's arguments". The same fix is repeated as a HARDENING_SUGGESTION (estimated lines changed: 4; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 0). (2 related items)
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:1460-1474 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The header comment says only a rejected dispatch, or a transient failure that used up the shared retry budget, leads to the plain fallback (`outcome=delta_fallback`). The code runs the fallback for any failed delta dispatch, including the `auth` and `other` classes, which are not retried.
  WHY: The comment does not match the code. It confuses maintainers and contradicts the inline documentation for the delta-fallback line.
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:1438 (single_pass_dispatch_audit) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: After a transient failure such as a network timeout in `gh workflow run`, the helper retries the dispatch without checking whether GitHub received and processed the first request.
  WHY: The concurrency group allows one running and one pending run with `cancel-in-progress: false` and does not deduplicate them, so a retry can queue a second audit run for the same PR and waste audit and runner capacity.
- TASK_GAP | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  Requirement: "The sentence about an old consumer wrapper appears only for `rejected`."
  Expected change site: scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh, both failed-dispatch body templates (exhausted-retry branch and non-exhausted branch)
  Evidence of absence: The hint is gated on class only in the non-exhausted branch (scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:1495). The exhausted-retry branch (scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:1479-1482) inserts `dispatch_error_sentence` but never appends `dispatch_wrapper_hint`, so a `rejected` failure there gets no wrapper-hint sentence.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- TASK_GAP | file: scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:the retry-exhausted body template at the "Single-issue security pass: retry audit" branch (PR diff context around lines 1476-1483), compared with the non-exhausted branch (PR diff context around line 1493-1496) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  Requirement: G3 from issue #10104: "The sentence about an old consumer wrapper appears only for `rejected`."
  Expected change site: the exhausted-retry body template in scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh
  Evidence of absence: The non-exhausted branch appends `dispatch_wrapper_hint` only when `dispatch_error_class = rejected`. The exhausted-retry branch builds `dispatch_error_sentence` but never appends a wrapper hint, so a `rejected` failure (HTTP 404/422, or "could not find any workflows") on the exhausted-head path gets no hint. This existed before the PR; the LAST RUN DIFF rewrote the surrounding header comment without addressing it.
- TASK_GAP | file: scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:header comment lines 139-148 and 167-173 (LAST RUN DIFF hunk; "Delta dispatch (gate)" paragraph) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  Requirement: Documentation accuracy: the header comment for the delta fallback should match the control flow at lines 1460-1474.
  Expected change site: scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh header comment, "Delta dispatch (gate)" paragraph
  Evidence of absence: The comment names only a rejected delta dispatch or a transient failure that used up the retry budget. The `else` branch at lines 1460-1474 has no `dispatch_error_class` gate, so `auth`, `other`, or a `rejected` failure not caused by the wrapper also falls back. Suggested wording: "Any failed delta dispatch (for example a consumer wrapper without the inputs, or a transient failure that used up the shared retry budget) is retried once".
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:363-384; .github/workflows/security-audit.yml:86-96 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A network error triggers another dispatch without checking whether GitHub accepted the first request.
  WHY: If GitHub accepts a dispatch but the response is lost, the helper classifies the error as `network` and retries. While the first audit is running, the per-PR concurrency group allows a pending run, so the retry can queue a second audit for the same PR and use more audit and runner capacity.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:lines 141-145 (header comment) vs lines 1468-1476 (fallback code) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The reworded header comment still lists only two causes for the plain fallback. The code at lines 1468-1476 takes the fallback after any failed delta dispatch, including `auth` (HTTP 401, or 403 without a rate-limit message) and `other` (e.g. HTTP 409, empty output). Line 170 is accurate; lines 141-143 are not.
  WHY: Documentation only, with no runtime failure. A maintainer would expect `auth`/`other` failures to skip the fallback, but the code makes the extra call and logs `outcome=delta_fallback dispatch_error=auth`. The fix is a one-line reword.
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:lines 366-385 (single_pass_dispatch_audit retry loop) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: After a `network`-classified failure, the helper retries `gh workflow run` without checking whether GitHub accepted the first dispatch. The per-PR audit concurrency group allows one running plus one queued run, so the retry can queue a second audit for the same head.
  WHY: This is bounded waste, not incorrectness: at most `SECURITY_PASS_DISPATCH_RETRIES` (default 2) extra dispatches, the latest marker per head/cycle wins, and the issue's Risks section accepts bounded extra calls. A stronger fix is outside this PR's non-goal boundary (#10017 throttle).
- TASK_GAP | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  Requirement: G3: "The sentence about an old consumer wrapper appears only for `rejected`."
  Expected change site: scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh, the exhausted-retry comment body template (lines 1488-1490), next to the non-exhausted template that gates the hint at lines 1502-1506.
  Evidence of absence: The exhausted-retry branch inserts `${dispatch_error_sentence}` but never defines or appends `${dispatch_wrapper_hint}`, so a `rejected` failure on the exhausted-head path gets no wrapper-hint sentence. The asymmetry existed before this PR; low impact and optional.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
